title: Degree bound and empty Proj criterion for an eventual coordinate polynomial
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $n\geq0$, and let $J\subseteq B=k[z_0,\ldots,z_n]$ be a homogeneous ideal for total degree, every variable having degree one. Give $A=B/J=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}A_d$ the quotient grading [def-sfb-coordinate-quotient-grading], and put $X=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj]. Suppose $Q\in\mathbf Q[x]$ and $d_0\geq0$ satisfy $Q(d)=\dim_k A_d$ for every integer $d\geq d_0$. Then $0\leq Q(d)\leq\binom{d+n}{n}$ for every $d\geq d_0$, and if $Q\ne0$, its leading coefficient is positive and $\deg Q\leq n$. Moreover, the following conditions are equivalent: $Q=0$; there exists $D\geq0$ such that $A_d=0$ for every $d\geq D$; and $X=\varnothing$. These conclusions include the unit ideal and the zero quotient ring, and require no reducedness or saturation hypothesis.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], the monomials $z_0^{\alpha_0}\cdots z_n^{\alpha_n}$ with $\sum_i\alpha_i=d$ are a basis of $B_d$. Their exponent vectors correspond bijectively to words of $d$ stars and $n$ bars: the successive star-block lengths are $\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_n$. Choosing the bar positions gives $\binom{d+n}{n}$ monomials, also when $n=0$ or $d=0$. By [def-sfb-coordinate-quotient-grading], their images span $A_d$. A basis extracted from this finite spanning family has at most this cardinality. Thus $A_d$ is finite-dimensional and $0\leq\dim_k A_d\leq\binom{d+n}{n}$. Substitute the assumed equality $Q(d)=\dim_k A_d$ for $d\geq d_0$.

source.place: Tag 08AC, lemma-hilbert-polynomial, subsequent paragraph: degree-d monomial count. Elementary stars-and-bars bijection and quotient spanning argument.

proof.text: Assume $Q\ne0$, and put $r=\deg Q$, $a=\operatorname{lc}(Q)\ne0$. Apply [lem-sfb-polynomial-leading-term-asymptotic] with $\epsilon=1/2$. For all sufficiently large positive integers $d$, $|Q(d)-ad^r|\leq |a|d^r/2$. If $a<0$, this implies $Q(d)\leq ad^r/2<0$, contradicting step 1; hence $a>0$ and $Q(d)\geq ad^r/2>0$ eventually. If $r>n$, then for $d\geq1$, step 1 gives $ad^r/2\leq\binom{d+n}{n}\leq(d+n)^n\leq(n+1)^n d^n$. The middle inequality follows directly from $\binom{d+n}{n}=\prod_{i=1}^n(d+i)/n!$, including the empty product. Cancel $d^n$: since $r-n\geq1$, this forces $ad/2\leq(n+1)^n$ for arbitrarily large integers $d$, impossible. Therefore $\deg Q\leq n$.

source.place: Agent growth argument attached to the monomial count following Tag 08AC; analytic input is the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: If $Q=0$, then for $d\geq d_0$ the finite-dimensional space $A_d$ has dimension zero, so it is zero: a nonzero vector would be linearly independent and extend to a nonempty basis. Conversely, if $A_d=0$ for $d\geq D$, then $Q(d)=0$ for all $d\geq\max(D,d_0)$. If $Q\ne0$, step 2 makes $Q(d)>0$ eventually, a contradiction. Thus $Q=0$ is equivalent to vanishing of the graded tail.

source.place: Elementary consequence of the eventual dimension equality and the positivity proved in step 2.

proof.text: Write $u_i$ for the image of $z_i$. The ideal $A_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}A_d$ is generated by the $u_i$: every positive-degree monomial contains a variable, and these monomials span every $A_d$. Consequently the opens $D_+(u_i)$ cover $X$ by the prime-ideal description in [def-pc-proj]. If $A_d=0$ for $d\geq D$, then $u_i^{\max(1,D)}=0$ for every $i$. A prime contains a nilpotent element, by repeated application of primality. Thus every homogeneous prime contains every $u_i$, hence $A_+$, so none is a point of $X$. This proves that a vanishing tail implies $X=\varnothing$.

source.place: Section-proj, standard opens; elementary prime-ideal argument for the degree-one generators.

proof.text: Conversely assume $X=\varnothing$. By [def-pc-proj], each $D_+(u_i)=\operatorname{Spec}(A_{(u_i)})$ is empty. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] to the zero ideal of the commutative ring $R=A_{(u_i)}$: the intersection of its empty family of prime ideals is $R$, so $1\in\sqrt{(0)}$, meaning $1^m=0$ for some $m\geq1$. Hence $1=0$ in $R$. By [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], this is the equality $1/1=0/1$ in the ordinary localization $A[1/u_i]$. Its fraction relation [def-weil-ring-localization-away] supplies $k_i\geq0$ with $u_i^{k_i}=0$ in $A$. Set $e_i=\max(1,k_i)$, so $e_i\geq1$ and $u_i^{e_i}=0$. This includes $u_i=0$ and the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology (1), (7); constructions.tex standard Proj charts; explicit localization fraction relation.

proof.text: Put $D=1+\sum_{i=0}^n(e_i-1)$. For $d\geq D$, a monomial $u_0^{\alpha_0}\cdots u_n^{\alpha_n}$ of degree $d$ has some $\alpha_i\geq e_i$: otherwise $d=\sum_i\alpha_i\leq\sum_i(e_i-1)=D-1$. Its factor $u_i^{e_i}$ makes it zero. These monomials span $A_d$ by [def-sfb-coordinate-quotient-grading] and [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], so $A_d=0$. Combining steps 3--5 gives all three equivalences. For the unit ideal every $A_d$ is zero; the argument has used neither reducedness nor saturation.
